answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, sized to exceed the profit from any single fake identity. Like a garden that only yields after seasons of careful tending, reputation accrues slowly from completed, verified work and decays after misbehavior, so launching a nebula of fresh clones buys no trust at all. An attacker must fund every willow-thin clone separately, and cheating forfeits its deposit, making mass fakery costlier than honest participation.
